rockhampton-6.bio: A free public art museum on Quay Street, opened in 2022 beside the Fitzroy River, with changing exhibitions and a collection.
unverified: Some special exhibitions are ticketed (third-party listing says $5 for one exhibition); general entry free per official page
opening year 2022 from a search snippet (Wikipedia/council), not re-read on the page
rockhampton-6.notes: Official page title 'Your Visit Rockhampton Museum of Art', 'Free entry'. Wikipedia address 212-214 Quay St; site says 220 Quay St.

rockhampton-7.bio: A domed 1899-1900 Classic Revival customs house on Quay Street, a highlight of Rockhampton's heritage building walk.
unverified: Whether the interior is open to visitors (council-tenanted offices; no visit page found): treat as exterior-only stop; owner may judge against COVERAGE test 2
rockhampton-7.notes: Tourism listing (ATDW) frames it as a photo stop on the CBD Heritage Walk; self-guided audio tour in Explore Rockhampton app. Built 1898-1901, Stanwell sandstone, copper dome (ATDW).

rockhampton-8.bio: A 50-hectare parkland of rainforest, waterfall and wetland walks on the Bruce Highway, with a playground and free camping.
rockhampton-8.notes: Council page: 'open to the public and there is no admission fee'; free parking. Council-run, not a park-pass park. Open parkland, no gate stated.

rockhampton-9.bio: A heritage-listed 1890s-1900s former railway station now a rail and steam tram museum on Denison Street.
unverified: Prices on the museum site are marked valid to 31 December 2026; check for 2027
rockhampton-9.notes: Adult $10, concession $7, child $6, family $30 (museum site). Site title 'Archer Park Rail Museum & Function Room'. 'Steam tram' detail from search snippet listing titles only: omit from bio if unsure.

capricorn-coast-4.bio: A 12-metre concrete and steel monument at Churchill's Lookout, Emu Park, that sings in the wind, honouring Cook's 1770 Keppel Bay voyage.
unverified: No official site found (council-owned monument); free/open inferred from it being a roadside lookout monument, not stated by a source
capricorn-coast-4.notes: Wikipedia: unveiled 30 May 1970, located at Churchill's Lookout on Constitution Hill.

gladstone-2.bio: A 14 km-long island sheltering Gladstone Harbour, reached by ferry from the marina, with 4WD tracks, beaches, fishing and camping.
unverified: Ferry fare not recorded (transport, not the price); not found on page
No single official site: Curtis Ferry Services is one operator; Gladstone Region tourism page BLOCKED for scripts
Camping permit needed at South End camping ground (from Gladstone Visitor Information Centre)
gladstone-2.notes: Ferry lands at Farmers Point; 4WD only on island (ferry page). Island pin is OSM waste facility (HIGH from two sources); owner may prefer a visitor point.

gladstone-3.bio: A large reservoir on the Boyne River about 30 km from Gladstone, with free picnic areas, walking trails, birdlife and barramundi fishing.
unverified: GAWB page does not state an entry fee; free rests on Wikipedia ('free recreation areas')
Pin is the dam wall; recreation area elsewhere on lake
gladstone-3.notes: Fishing may need Queensland stocked impoundment permit (SIPS) - unverified, not a cost of the spot.

gladstone-5.bio: A 1930s former town hall in Goondoon Street housing a free regional art gallery and museum of local history.
gladstone-5.notes: Official site title 'Gladstone Regional Art Gallery and Museum | GRAGM', 'FREE ENTRY'. Built 1933-34, Queensland Heritage Register 1998 (Wikipedia).

gladstone-6.bio: Gladstone's council-run botanic gardens, with the Crown of Gold tree, a bonsai house and free guided garden tours.
unverified: Gated/hours not recorded; 'entry' chosen as a staffed garden - owner may prefer open
gladstone-6.notes: Council page: 'Entry to the Botanic Gardens is free'; Yujo Bonsai House, Crown of Gold tree.

gladstone-8.bio: An open-air museum of over 20 heritage buildings and collections by the Calliope River, with a kiosk and a large country market.
unverified: $5 adult from ExplorOz directory only, undated; official site shows no price
Village open 9am-3pm except Wednesday and Saturday until further notice (not for bio)
gladstone-8.notes: Official site title 'Calliope River Historical Village'; 'over 20 museums & collections'. gladstoneregion.info page BLOCKED (captcha).
